items.prompt: Which animal is an invertebrate, with no backbone?

options.why: Fish have a backbone.
Birds have a backbone.
Cats have a backbone.

hints: Invertebrates have no bones inside.
Think about which animal is soft with a shell.
Which animal could you not feel a backbone in?
items.explanation: A snail has no backbone, so it is an invertebrate. Fish, birds and cats are vertebrates.

items.prompt: Sort the animals into vertebrates and invertebrates.
hints: Vertebrates have a backbone.
Insects, spiders and crabs have an exoskeleton instead.
Start with the shark. Does it have a backbone?
items.explanation: Frogs, snakes, ducks and sharks have backbones. Spiders, butterflies, earthworms and crabs are invertebrates.

items.prompt: Match each vertebrate group to its features.
pairs: moist skin, live in water and on land
hair or fur, feed babies milk
hints: Think of one example animal for each group.
A frog is an amphibian and a snake is a reptile.
Which group feeds its babies milk?
items.explanation: Fish have gills, fins and scales, and amphibians have moist skin. Reptiles have dry scales, birds have feathers and mammals have hair and feed their babies milk.

items.prompt: Use the key. An animal has no legs and no shell. What is it?

figure.caption: Key to four minibeasts
head: Question
Yes
No
figure.alt: A key. Question 1: Does it have legs? Yes, go to 2. No, go to 3. Question 2: Does it have 6 legs? Yes, ant. No, spider. Question 3: Does it have a shell? Yes, snail. No, earthworm.

options.why: An ant has 6 legs.
A spider has 8 legs.
A snail has a shell.

hints: Start at question 1 every time.
No legs sends you to question 3.
Now answer question 3 for this animal.
items.explanation: No legs takes you to question 3. No shell gives the answer: an earthworm.

items.prompt: Use the key. A bird cannot fly. What is it?

figure.caption: Key to five animals
head: Question
Yes
No
figure.alt: A key. 1: Does it have feathers? Yes, go to 2. No, go to 3. 2: Can it fly? Yes, owl. No, penguin. 3: Does it have fur? Yes, rabbit. No, go to 4. 4: Does it have fins? Yes, fish. No, frog.

options.why: An owl can fly.
A rabbit has fur, not feathers.
A frog has no feathers.

hints: All birds have feathers.
Feathers send you to question 2.
Answer question 2 for a bird that cannot fly.
items.explanation: Feathers take you to question 2. It cannot fly, so the key gives penguin.

items.prompt: Which question in the key tells a frog apart from a fish?

figure.caption: Key to five animals
head: Question
Yes
No
figure.alt: A key. 1: Does it have feathers? Yes, go to 2. No, go to 3. 2: Can it fly? Yes, owl. No, penguin. 3: Does it have fur? Yes, rabbit. No, go to 4. 4: Does it have fins? Yes, fish. No, frog.

options.why: Neither a frog nor a fish has feathers, so question 1 does not split them.
Question 2 is only for animals with feathers.
Neither has fur, so question 3 does not split them.

hints: Follow the key for a frog, then for a fish.
Find the first question where their answers are different.
A fish has fins. Does a frog?
items.explanation: A frog and a fish both answer no to questions 1 and 3. Question 4 splits them, because only the fish has fins.

items.prompt: Animals without a backbone are called ___.
hints: Snails, worms and insects belong to this group.
In- at the start of a word can mean not.
The word starts with in.
items.explanation: Animals without a backbone are invertebrates. Insects, spiders, snails and worms are invertebrates.

items.prompt: Bats fly and have wings, but they are mammals. Why?

options.why: Bats give birth to live babies.

options.text: They have fur and feed their babies milk.

options.why: Bats have no feathers. Their wings are made of skin.
Where an animal lives does not decide its group.

hints: Flying does not decide the group.
Remember the features of mammals.
What covers a bat's body?
items.explanation: Bats have fur and feed their babies milk, so they are mammals. Their wings are made of skin, not feathers.

items.prompt: Look at the Carroll diagram. Where does a crab belong?

figure.alt: Carroll diagram. Vertebrates with legs: cat, frog. Vertebrates with no legs: fish, snake. Invertebrates with legs: spider, ant. Invertebrates with no legs: earthworm, snail.

options.why: A crab has no backbone. Its skeleton is on the outside.
A crab has ten legs, counting its claws.
A crab has legs and no backbone.

hints: Answer two questions about a crab.
Does a crab have a backbone?
Does a crab have legs?
items.explanation: A crab has an exoskeleton and no backbone, so it is an invertebrate. It has legs, so it goes with the spider and the ant.

items.prompt: Which question splits spider, ant, fish and cat into two groups of two?

options.why: Only the fish has no legs, so you get groups of 3 and 1.
Only the spider has 8 legs.
All four are living things, so this does not split them.

hints: Try each question on all four animals.
Count the yes answers for each question.
You need exactly two yes answers.
items.explanation: Fish and cats have backbones, and spiders and ants do not. So this question makes two groups of two.

items.prompt: Choose 3 animals that are mammals.

options.why: Penguins have feathers and lay eggs. They are birds.
Sharks are fish. They breathe with gills.

hints: Mammals have hair or fur and feed their babies milk.
Some mammals live in the sea or fly.
Do not be tricked by where an animal lives.
items.explanation: Whales, bats and monkeys are mammals because they feed their babies milk. Penguins are birds and sharks are fish.

items.prompt: Write a key with yes or no questions. It must identify a snail, a spider and a bird.

criteria.label: Uses questions that can be answered yes or no
The first question splits the animals into two groups
Each animal ends up on its own

items.model: 1. Does it have feathers? Yes: bird. No: go to 2. 2. Does it have legs? Yes: spider. No: snail.
hints: Find one feature that only one animal has.
Each question should split a group into smaller groups.
items.explanation: A good key splits the animals step by step. For example, ask: Does it have feathers? Then ask: Does it have legs?

items.prompt: Which group of animals has feathers?

options.why: Fish have scales, not feathers.
Most mammals have fur or hair.
Reptiles have dry scaly skin.

hints: Think about a chicken or an owl.
Feathers help these animals fly.
They also lay eggs with hard shells.
items.explanation: Birds are the only animals with feathers.

items.prompt: Which group of animals breathes underwater using gills?

options.why: Birds breathe air with lungs.
Mammals breathe air with lungs, even whales and dolphins.
Reptiles breathe air with lungs.

hints: Gills take oxygen from water.
Think about animals that live only in water.
These animals also have fins and scales.
items.explanation: Fish have gills to take oxygen from the water.

items.prompt: Sort the animals into the correct group.
hints: Reptiles have dry scaly skin.
Amphibians have smooth, damp skin.
Mammals feed milk to their babies, even in the sea.
items.explanation: A dolphin is a mammal even though it lives in water. Frogs, toads and newts are amphibians. Crocodiles and geckos are reptiles.

items.prompt: Tap the animal that has no backbone.

figure.alt: Four animals in a row: a bird, a fish, a snail and a frog.

hints: An animal with a backbone is a vertebrate.
Fish, birds and frogs all have a backbone.
Look for the soft animal with a shell.
items.explanation: A snail has no backbone, so it is an invertebrate.

items.prompt: Label the parts of this insect.

figure.alt: Side view of an insect with three body sections in a row. A round head with two thin feelers is on the left, a middle section has three legs, and a long oval back section is on the right.

hints: An insect has three body sections in a line.
The first section holds the eyes and feelers.
The legs are joined to the middle section.
items.explanation: An insect has a head, a thorax and an abdomen. It also has six legs joined to the thorax.

items.prompt: Look at the Venn diagram. A butterfly has wings and 6 legs. Where does it go?

figure.alt: Venn diagram with two circles, has wings and has 6 legs. Bird is in has wings only. Bee is where the circles overlap. Ant is in has 6 legs only. Snail is outside both circles.

options.why: It also has 6 legs, so it belongs in both circles.
It also has wings, so it belongs in both circles.
It has both features, so it cannot be outside.

hints: Check each circle one at a time.
Does a butterfly have wings? Does it have 6 legs?
If both are yes, where does it go?
items.explanation: A butterfly has wings and 6 legs, so it goes in the overlap with the bee.

items.prompt: Fill in the table with yes or no.
items.caption: Animal features
head: Animal
Backbone
Wings
hints: Sharks have a backbone but no wings.
A beetle has no backbone.
Use yes or no in each blank.
items.explanation: A beetle has no backbone. A shark has a backbone but no wings. An earthworm has no backbone.

items.prompt: Pia says, "A whale is a fish because it lives in the sea." Which fact shows it is a mammal?

options.why: Many animals live in the sea. Where it lives does not decide its group.
Fish and many other animals have tails too.

options.text: It breathes air and feeds its babies milk

options.why: Size does not decide the group.

hints: Where an animal lives does not tell you its group.
Look at how it breathes and feeds its young.
Fish have gills. Does a whale?
items.explanation: A whale breathes air with lungs and feeds its young on milk. These are features of mammals.

items.prompt: The questions in a key can be answered with yes or ___.
hints: A key uses two possible answers.
It is the opposite of yes.
It has two letters.
items.explanation: Each question in a key has two answers: yes or no.

items.prompt: Put these animals in order from fewest legs to most legs.
hints: Start with the animal that has no legs.
A bird has two legs and a dog has four.
An ant has six legs and a spider has eight.
items.explanation: A snake has 0 legs, a bird 2, a dog 4, an ant 6 and a spider 8.

items.prompt: A class finds 3 spiders, 5 beetles, 4 sparrows, 2 frogs and 6 worms. How many have no backbone?
hints: Spiders, beetles and worms have no backbone.
Sparrows and frogs have a backbone.
Add the three groups with no backbone.
items.explanation: 3 + 5 + 6 = 14 animals with no backbone.

items.prompt: Use the key. An animal has 6 legs and no wings. What is it?

figure.caption: Key to five small animals
head: Question
Yes
No
figure.alt: A key. Question 1: Does it have legs? Yes go to 3, no go to 2. Question 2: Does it have a shell? Yes snail, no earthworm. Question 3: Does it have 6 legs? Yes go to 4, no spider. Question 4: Does it have wings? Yes bee, no ant.

options.why: A bee has wings.
A spider has 8 legs, not 6.
An earthworm has no legs.

hints: Start at question 1.
Yes to legs sends you to question 3.
Follow the answers about 6 legs and then wings.
items.explanation: Legs: yes (go to 3). 6 legs: yes (go to 4). Wings: no. The animal is an ant.

items.prompt: Mia uses the key on a butterfly (6 legs and wings). What does the key say, and what does this show?

figure.caption: Key to five small animals
head: Question
Yes
No
figure.alt: A key. Question 1: Does it have legs? Yes go to 3, no go to 2. Question 2: Does it have a shell? Yes snail, no earthworm. Question 3: Does it have 6 legs? Yes go to 4, no spider. Question 4: Does it have wings? Yes bee, no ant.

options.text: It says ant, so the key is correct
options.why: A butterfly has wings, so the key does not send it to ant.

options.text: It says bee, so the key needs another question
It says spider, so the key is correct
options.why: A butterfly has 6 legs, so the key does not send it to spider.

options.text: It says snail, so the key is correct
options.why: A butterfly has legs and no shell, so the key does not send it to snail.

hints: Follow the key with a butterfly.
Check what name you reach at the end.
Ask whether a butterfly really is that animal.
items.explanation: The key ends at bee because it has no question that separates a bee from a butterfly. A good key needs a new question.

items.prompt: Choose 3 features that all insects have.

options.why: Eight legs is a feature of spiders.
Insects have no backbone.
Insects have hard outer cases, not fur.

hints: Think about an ant, a bee and a beetle.
Count their legs and body sections.
Insects have no backbone and no fur.
items.explanation: All insects have six legs, three body sections and a pair of feelers.

items.prompt: Match each animal to its group.
hints: A penguin cannot fly but it has feathers.
A gecko has dry scaly skin.
A frog starts life in water.
items.explanation: A whale is a mammal, a frog is an amphibian, a gecko is a reptile and a penguin is a bird.

items.prompt: A key is a set of ___ that helps us to name a living thing. Each answer leads to another ___ or to a name.
hints: A key is made of questions.
The word for the second gap is also a thing we ask.
Pick the same word, but singular.
items.explanation: A key is a set of questions. Each answer leads to the next question or to the name of the living thing.

items.prompt: Citra makes a key for leaves. Which question is best for her key?

options.why: People may not agree on what is pretty, so it is hard to answer.
Almost every leaf is green, so it does not split the leaves.
This is about opinion, not a feature of the leaf.

options.text: Is the edge of the leaf smooth?

hints: A good key question has a clear answer.
It should split the group into two parts.
Choose a feature you can see and check.
items.explanation: A good question can be checked by looking, and it splits the leaves into two groups. Smooth or not is clear.

items.prompt: True or false: A fish and a frog can be put into different groups.
hints: Do both have the same skin?
One has fins and the other legs.
Different groups.
items.explanation: Fish live in water all their lives and have fins, and most have scales. Frogs are amphibians with smooth, moist skin and live in water and on land.

items.prompt: True or false: A spider is an insect because it is small.
hints: Count the legs.
Do insects have eight legs?
Spiders have eight legs.
items.explanation: Insects have six legs. A spider has eight legs, so it is an arachnid. Being small does not decide the group.

items.prompt: True or false: A key is a set of questions that helps you identify a living thing.
hints: Think of a branching set of questions.
Each answer narrows the choices.
A key uses questions.
items.explanation: Each question has a yes or no answer that leads you to the next question until you reach the name.
